notes.text:
# Known Relative Norm Removes The Prime-Conductor Quantum Opening

**2026-11-06 scope refresh:** the repeated-character composite-conductor
phase problem is now covered by Tal's September classical algorithm,
ECCC TR26-211, Theorem1.5/Section3.1, and the reviewed group-ring reduction
in [JACOBI_GROUP_RING_RECOVERY.md](JACOBI_GROUP_RING_RECOVERY.md). Do not
use this older note's unextended prime-primary proof to infer that the
corresponding repeated-Jacobi task still needs a quantum phase routine.
This does not promote the old LLL implementation to full norm recovery.

2026-10-17. Published classical theorem, local application REVIEW PENDING.
This supersedes the suggestion that growing-conductor LLL success is the
decisive unresolved question for this particular surface-counting proposal.
It does not assert that a Gentry-Szydlo implementation exists in the repo.

## Question And Decision

The [surface experiment](JACOBI_SURFACE_RECONSTRUCTION.md) proposed quantum
principal-ideal/unit recovery from public Jacobi carries. Generic principal
ideal problems can be hard. But this input also supplies the exact relative
norm, J*bar(J)=p^2. That additional information changes the computational
problem. Comparing only generic PIP or empirical LLL success misses the
appropriate classical competitor.

[Lenstra and Silverberg, Testing isomorphism of lattices over CM-orders,
1706.07373v3](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.07373), Theorem 1.3, gives a
deterministic classical polynomial-time decision AND recovery algorithm for
an ideal and prescribed relative norm in a CM-order, when the polarized
ideal identity holds. No GRH assumption is part of that theorem. Its
Algorithms 18.6/18.7 establish the recovery assertion, not merely a test of
the principal-ideal class. The factorization in Algorithm 18.1 is of a
constructed integer with bounded small prime factors, not a free generic
integer-factorization oracle.

**Decision:** for odd prime conductor and the stated public split-root
input, this published theorem plus the Jacobi identities and primary
congruence gives classical polynomial-time exact surface counting in
ell and log p. The proposed asymptotic quantum advantage is therefore not
a credible target under those premises. Do not continue this route by
searching for LLL failures or implementing known quantum PIP primitives.
This is a prior-art application, NOT a new classical algorithm claim.

## Direct Reduction To Theorem 1.3

Inputs: odd prime ell, prime p with ell|(p-1), explicit order-ell eta mod p,
and admissible nontrivial character exponents a,b,c with a+b+c nonzero mod ell.
Use A=Z[zeta_ell] and the POSITIVE embeddings zeta -> eta^t. All data are
explicit integers; no coherent oracle, true Jacobi value or field-sized
character table is an input.

1. A is a CM-order. In the basis 1,zeta,...,zeta^(ell-2), the multiplication
   table and conjugation matrix have polynomial size and integer entries.
2. Build I from the public split-prime powers P_t^e_t, with
   e_t=2-floor(((at mod ell)+(bt mod ell)+(ct mod ell))/ell).
   A basis follows from modular evaluation kernels at the lifted split roots.
3. Conjugation sends P_t to P_(-t). Since e_t+e_(-t)=2, we have
   I*bar(I)=product_t P_t^2=p^2*A. Set w=p^2, a totally positive scalar.
4. The Jacobi ideal identity gives I=(J); the Weil identity gives
   J*bar(J)=p^2. These establish the YES promise. IMPORTANT: the identity
   I*bar(I)=w*A by itself is NOT a proof that a normalized generator exists.
5. The published algorithm returns v with I=A*v and v*bar(v)=p^2.
   The ratio v/J is an algebraic unit with relative norm1. Every embedding
   has absolute value1; Kronecker's theorem makes it a root of unity.
6. For odd prime ell the root group is {+/-zeta^k}. The established primary
   condition J=1 mod(1-zeta)^2 identifies the correct one by testing
   A(1)=1, A'(1)=0 mod ell. This needs no quantum phase estimate.
7. Recover the at most (ell-1)^3 admissible sums, combine their explicit
   multiplicities and add p^2+p+1. No prime-square residue reconstruction or
   generic compact-output local division is needed on this classical route.

Each ideal contains p^2*A. Its canonical HNF basis has coefficient bit size
O(log p). The order has rank ell-1 and polynomial-size structure constants;
the whole theorem input has size polynomial in ell and log p. The output
also has polynomial size: writing J=sum_(j<ell-1) a_j*zeta^j, the known norm
implies ell*sum a_j^2-(sum a_j)^2=(ell-1)*p^2. The trace Gram's smallest
eigenvalue is1, so each |a_j|<=sqrt(ell-1)*p.

Thus enumeration of the character triples and root choices remains
polynomial in ell and log p. An explicit ell=poly(log p) promise suffices
for polynomial succinct-input time. Without it, neither the earlier quantum
proposal nor this reduction is claimed polynomial in log ell. This is a
complexity comparison, not an implementation/performance crossover claim.

## Independent Group-Ring Check

To avoid confusing the CM theorem with a generic-PIP solver, we also
construct an explicit input to the older Gentry-Szydlo setting.
[Lattices with Symmetry](https://arxiv.org/html/1501.00178), Remark 8.6,
explains the polynomial recovery of a generator from its ideal and cyclic
autocorrelation in R=Z[X]/(X^ell-1), ell odd prime.

Let J have canonical coefficients a_0,...,a_(ell-2), and pad a_(ell-1)=0.
Since sum a_j=1 mod ell and p=1 mod ell, the integer
c=(p-sum a_j)/ell exists. The lift v has coefficients a_j+c at all ell
positions. It projects to J and has augmentation v(1)=p.

The cyclic product v*bar(v)-p^2 vanishes in the cyclotomic quotient, so is
a multiple of Phi_ell in R. Its augmentation is0, hence that multiple is0.
Thus v has exactly known cyclic autocorrelation (p^2,0,...,0).

The public R-ideal imposes the SAME split-root carry constraints plus
augmentation divisible by p. Its index is p^(sum e_t+1)=p^ell. The principal
ideal (v) is contained in it and also has index
|v(1)*Norm_K(J)|=p^ell, proving equality. This proves the GS YES promise
without using v to construct the actual public basis.

For basis B, the normalized Gram B*B^T/p^2 is positive definite, integral
and unimodular. Cyclic shift has an explicit integral isometry matrix.
The cyclic order-2ell group is represented by -shift, whose ell-th power
is -I, matching the signed group-ring convention. Ordinary cyclotomic
trace Grams instead have determinant ell^(ell-2), NOT1; the two encodings
must not be silently interchanged. Group symmetry is supplied, not inferred
from an arbitrary unimodular lattice.

## Executed Evidence And Nonimplementation

Run:

```text
python theorems/jacobi_known_norm_reduction.py --write
python -m pytest -q tests/test_jacobi_known_norm_reduction.py tests/test_jacobi_surface_reconstruction.py
```

The producer builds both theorem inputs for six native controls and all51
distinct ideal profiles at p=2^61-1, ell11. It verifies exact product-ideal
HNF, normalized Gram positivity/determinants, module actions, signed cyclic
action, augmentation and index. The large inputs require no character
table, LLL, true Jacobi sum or phase estimate. The six small known-generator
lifts are separately charged CALIBRATIONS, not input constructors.
The reused reference source caps conductors at24 and primes below2^64;
these implementation caps are not assumptions of the symbolic reduction
or of the imported theorem, and exceeding them is not evidence of hardness.

Tests include an independent SymPy product-lattice HNF and matrix replay,
direct cyclic autocorrelations, all small admissible symmetric triples,
wrong norms, nonideal lattices with the right index, non-root unit
contamination and opposite-character conventions. A valid polarized input
is never labeled a solved instance just because those checks pass.

**Not executed:** the Lenstra-Silverberg auxiliary-ideal/tensor-power
generator-recovery algorithm. Existing actual surface reconstruction still
uses LLL plus exact primary normalization; its failure remains UNKNOWN for
that implementation. The asymptotic conclusion imports the published
classical theorem and depends on the stated local reduction proof, not on
finite success or a relabeling of LLL as GS. Local application has not had
independent human/formal review. No central candidate, proof or general
negative-result promotion is made automatically.

## Attempt To Falsify This Conclusion

- **Wrong theorem problem?** Theorem 1.3 requires the norm, not just the
  ideal. Here the norm is exactly the public scalar p^2. If the application
  supplied only an unknown positive unit times p^2, this reduction would
  fail. Native checks and the Jacobi Weil identity rule that out here.
- **Invalid ideal/involution?** Carry orientation matters. Every product
  ideal is checked exactly, and inverse-label inputs are retained as distinct
  valid inputs, not confused with the intended J. A carry or ideal-identity
  counterexample would invalidate the local application.
- **Norm identity implies existence?** It does not in general. This family
  has a concrete Jacobi witness analytically; arbitrary polarized ideals
  cannot inherit the YES conclusion. Native small witnesses independently
  check that premise but are not a proof for all inputs.
- **Uncharged number-theory oracle?** A verified eta is part of both input
  models; neither algorithm gets a hidden root for free. The imported
  theorem is unconditional deterministic polynomial time in its explicit
  input size, not a heuristic unit-group/PIP subroutine. Efficient public
  ideal construction and polynomial output size are shown above.
- **Root ambiguity still hard?** Prime-primary normalization removes it
  without evaluating J. This pass does NOT extend that step to all composite
  conductors. A counterexample to the prime-primary proof would reopen
  exact identification, not make generic normalized recovery quantum-hard.
- **Does this refute a recent quantum paper?** No. The repo's specific
  prime-conductor surface target is narrower than external claims and may
  have different output/input conventions. No author-error conclusion is
  inferred from a missing citation or this local reduction alone.

## Next Research Action

Retire this prime-conductor proposal as an asymptotic advantage target,
subject to independent review of the application. Keep its arithmetic
tests as reusable falsifiers. Do not spend main-model research budget
implementing a known GS algorithm solely to reproduce its theorem.

Before any broader arithmetic pivot, require a specific output NOT already

independent constructive mechanisms. Unknown norms or ambiguous composite
roots are not automatically hard tasks, and failure of LLL is not evidence
that a quantum algorithm is needed. A new candidate must have an explicit
end-to-end task and strongest known classical comparison first.

reduction for split Fermat SURFACES, and what can a serious classical attack
already reconstruct? This is a candidate reduction experiment, not a new
end-to-end quantum implementation or a refutation of the cited papers.

## Problem, Input And Intended Advantage

Count projective solutions over F_p of

    X^d + Y^d + Z^d = W^d,      p prime, d>=3, d|(p-1).

p and d are public binary integers. A verified order-d root eta in F_p is
public, not a hidden function. The character is defined by
chi(x)=zeta_d^j when x^((p-1)/d)=eta^j; a table of size d, not p, implements
this evaluator. The EXHAUSTIVE native reference additionally makes a size-p
table, explicitly charged and never used by the public-ideal attack.

The proposed quantum target is polynomial in d and log p, NOT polynomial
in log d. To get a polynomial succinct-input algorithm, require an explicit
growth promise d=poly(log p). Fixed d already has strong classical arithmetic
methods and cannot establish an asymptotic separation. No classical lower
bound or best-known-algorithm separation is claimed for growing d here.

The prospective mechanism is a carry-described cyclotomic ideal, a real
principal-ideal/unit reconstruction, exact local residues and an integer
point-count lift. No coherent hidden oracle, source preparation assumption
or free full-field sum is part of that proposed pipeline. The quantum
principal-ideal/unit routines and generic three-character extension have
NOT been implemented or independently reviewed by this pass.

## Exact Reduction

Let J(a,b,c)=sum_(x+y+z=1) chi^a(x)chi^b(y)chi^c(z), extending ALL characters
by zero at0. For a,b,c in1..d-1 with a+b+c !=0 mod d,

    #surface = p^2+p+1 + C,
    C = sum_(admissible ordered triples) J(a,b,c).

Character orthogonality gives this projective formula. The number of terms is
B=(d-1)(d^2-3d+3), and each has absolute value p. Thus |C|<=Bp. C is an
integer, not an approximate complex number. If p>2B, C mod p^2 has a unique
lift in [-Bp,Bp]. If p<=2B=O(d^3), a full-field classical convolution count
costs polynomial time in d. The prototype rejects ambiguous residues rather
than silently using centered rounding. It explicitly counts the projective
boundary, not just the affine chart.

All triple sums are computed by exact two-character sums and a convolution
identity. When a+b=0, the missing zero-convolution mass matters:
J(a,-a,c)=p*chi^a(-1). Dropping it changes the norm and the point count.

## Ideal And Valuation Conventions

Use K=Q(zeta_d), the monic cyclotomic integral basis, and POSITIVE reductions
zeta_d -> eta^t, t in(Z/dZ)^*. The generalized Stickelberger carry profile is

    e_t = 2-floor(((at mod d)+(bt mod d)+(ct mod d))/d).

It satisfies e_t+e_(-t)=2 and sum e_t=phi(d). The inverse-root convention
has complementary carries; copying its labels would be wrong. Every native
sum is checked at all split primes modulo p^3, including exact valuations2.
Teichmuller roots use eta_t^(p^(h-1)) mod p^h. The exact relative norm is
J*conjugate(J)=p^2 in the FIELD, not merely a floating magnitude at one place.

To reduce J/p^v to h unit digits requires h+v input digits. The native helper
demonstrates this and rejects inversion of p modulo p^h. It does NOT implement
valuation-aware division of arbitrary compact quantum outputs. That bit-cost
extension is still an explicit obligation; known repeated-character residue
theorems must not silently be treated as arbitrary three-character routines.

claiming LLL/Jacobi reconstruction as new:
[Buhler and Koblitz (1998)](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bulletin-of-the-australian-mathematical-society/article/lattice-basis-reduction-jacobi-sums-and-hyperelliptic-cryptosystems/211979CB954028EF8899B3FB49930091)

## Prime Conductors Need No Phase Oracle

For odd prime conductor ell, lambda=1-zeta_ell, the THREE-character sum obeys

    J(a,b,c) = 1 mod lambda^2.

Elementary derivation: expand zeta^e=1-e*lambda modulo lambda^2. The number

divisible by ell, since sum_(x!=0) log_chi(x) is divisible by ell for odd ell.
As ell is divisible by lambda^(ell-1), both required congruences follow.

In Z[zeta_ell]/lambda^2, test A(1)=1 and A'(1)=0 mod ell. The2ell roots of
unity have distinct residues in this quotient. Thus this primary condition
selects the correct root multiple of a balanced generator CLASSICALLY, with
no phase estimate or true character sum. It does not replace norm
normalization: multiplying by the non-root unit1+zeta_5 preserves the ideal
but fails the relative-norm test. Composite conductors are not covered by
this implemented primary-normalization proof.

# Native RLWE Graph Kernels and Quaternion Orders

2026-10-05. LOCAL DERIVATION / REVIEW PENDING. No independent theorem review,
new quantum algorithm, efficient quaternion generator, novelty or speedup claim.

SELF-CRITIQUE FOLLOW-UP: [the conductor-order audit](NATIVE_RLWE_CONDUCTOR_ORDER_AUDIT.md)
constructs a different fractional ideal encoding that preserves the ORIGINAL
metric exactly. Its direct PIP route fails instead through global principality,
and extension to an ambient overorder erases the generic source's level data.
The metric-lift obstruction here must not be generalized to that construction.

## Research Question

Can the actual native rank-two kernel acquire useful quaternionic structure,
rather than merely invoke number-field principal ideals on one existing line?
Yes, it admits an explicit label-adaptive definite quaternion order. But the
encoding changes the metric, has no general principality promise, and supplies
no generator algorithm. An alternative always-principal encoding supplies its
own generator, which need not be short. These are distinct constructions.

This is an algebraic audit, not a proof that quaternion methods cannot work.
The potentially valuable remaining primitive is a costed, source-valid short
element algorithm for the definite order, with transfer to the ORIGINAL metric.

## 1. Actual Native Input

Let R=Z[X]/(X^d+1), d a power of two, K=Q(zeta_(2d)), and bar complex
conjugation. Coefficient vectors satisfy

```
bar(a)=(a_0,-a_(d-1),...,-a_1), C_bar(a)=C_a^T.
Lambda_M={(g,f) in R^2: g=Mf mod q}.
B=[qI,C_M;0,I], det(B)=q^d.
```

The saved d64 Babai certificate instead uses public matrix [I,C_m^T] and
columns [qI,-C_m^T;0,I]. Set M=bar(m) and (g,f)=(x,-y). This is an exact
signed isometry, not a metric approximation. All 128 saved reduced basis rows
are checked after this map. No LLL rerun or favorable source reroll is used.

## 2. Strong Original-Metric Gate

Assume q is prime, q=3 mod8, and d>=4. Consider ANY K-conjugate-semilinear
operator J on K^2 satisfying J^2=-I, preserving both Lambda_M and its original
product coefficient metric. The operator may depend on M. Then

```
Such a J exists if and only if M*bar(M)=-1 mod q.
```

Proof sketch, including integrality rather than just a fixed-axis test:

1. Write J=Z composed with conjugation. The coefficient norm is the normalized
   field trace of the Hermitian norm. Polarization over K implies Z is unitary.
   From Z*bar(Z)=-I and Z^-1=bar(Z)^T, obtain Z^T=-Z. Thus
   Z=[0,h;-h,0], h*bar(h)=1. This includes rational, nonintegral adaptive h.
2. Applying J to (M,1) gives h*(1+M*bar(M)) in qR. Write beta=1+M*bar(M).
   Norm_K(h)=1, so integrality forces q^d to divide Norm_K(beta).
3. In this CRT regime R/qR is E x E, |E|=q^(d/2), with conjugation swapping
   the two factors. Its conjugation-fixed subring is a FIELD E. Since beta is
   real, any nonzero residue is a unit in R/qR, contradicting that divisibility.
   Hence beta=0 mod q. This argument also covers nonunit original ratios.
4. Now M is a unit modulo q. Applying J to (q,0) first gives qh in R and
   Mqh in qR, hence h in R. The identity h*bar(h)=1 forces coefficient norm
   squared one, so h is a signed monomial. There is no free rational phase.
5. Conversely J_0(g,f)=(-bar(f),bar(g)) is an original-metric isometry with
   square -I and preserves the graph exactly when beta=0 mod q.

For IID full-ring public ratios the compatible count is |E|-1 among |E|^2.
Its probability is (q^(d/2)-1)/q^d < q^(-d/2); conditioned on a unit ratio it
is 1/(q^(d/2)-1). The existing d12 source parameters give conservative dyadic
upper exponents 2304,12288,61440 at d64,256,1024. Primality is an explicit
external certificate obligation, NOT established by this module's congruence
test. The d2 Gaussian case is different: q3 has four eligible ratios out of
nine. Low-CRT q=1 mod8 is also outside this probability formula.

Scope: K-conjugate-semilinear Hamilton structure preserving the stated metric
and R-action. NOT arbitrary Q-linear structures, different R-actions, weighted
orders, all quantum algorithms, RLWE security, or a general lattice lower bound.

## 3. An Explicit Definite Quaternion Order

Choose a real, totally positive rho in R with rho=-M*bar(M) mod q. Define

```
O_rho=R + R*j, j*a=bar(a)*j, j^2=-rho.
(g,f)*(h,k)=(gh-rho*f*bar(k), gk+f*bar(h)).
nrd(g,f)=g*bar(g)+rho*f*bar(f).
J_rho(g,f)=(-rho*bar(f),bar(g)), J_rho^2=-rho I.
```

Lambda_M is a LEFT O_rho ideal because rho+M*bar(M)=0 mod q. Right closure
is not automatic: a d2/q3/M=1+i countercontrol rejects two-sided treatment.
The construction uses R directly; it does not assume an unjustified integral
decomposition O_K=O_F[i] for a CM field.

Actual positive lift: center the coefficients of -M*bar(M) modulo odd q,
then add a scalar q-multiple until rho_0-sum_(i>0)|rho_i|>=1. Centering
preserves conjugation. C_rho is real symmetric. Gershgorin gives exact bounds
L=rho_0-sum|rho_i| and U=rho_0+sum|rho_i|. Therefore

```
||g||^2+||f||^2 <= ||g||^2+f^T C_rho f
                    <= max(1,U)*(||g||^2+||f||^2).
```

The lift is polynomial-bit and genuinely definite. But its distortion can
grow with q. A weighted-short output is not automatically sufficiently short
for native decoding or for the reciprocal-energy completion criteria. Ideal
principality is unproved in general. In the special case where this parameter
equals the next principal construction, principality IS known; do not suppress
that easy positive branch. Neither case supplies a new quantum primitive.

## 4. Always Principal Does Not Mean Useful

Instead choose rho=q-M*bar(M) and alpha=(M,1). Then nrd(alpha)=q. Right
multiplication by alpha has the exact column basis

```
[C_M,-C_rho;I,C_M^T].
C_M*C_M^T+C_rho=qI.
```

It lies in the graph and has determinant q^d, so Lambda_M=O_rho*alpha.
The generator is ALREADY KNOWN; PIP does not have a hidden generator to find.
This rho is not necessarily positive. If rho=0 the algebra is degenerate,
not a central-simple quaternion algebra or a legitimate quaternion-PIP input.
The d4/q3/M=(1,1,0,1) control has precisely this degeneracy.

Exact shortness countercontrol: d2, q257, M128. The known generator has
physical norm squared 16385, while (-1,2) belongs to the kernel with norm
squared 5. Here rho=257-128^2<0. Every principal generator must have reduced
norm +/-257, because the center is Q and its multiplication determinant is
the square of that norm. A generator with f=0 is impossible: g is divisible
by q. For f!=0 its coefficient norm obeys

```
||g||^2 = nrd + (128^2-257)*||f||^2 >= 128^2-2*257=15870.
```

Thus EVERY principal generator is much longer than the available relation,
not just an unfortunate choice of generator. This is a structured d2 transfer
counterexample, not a native-average or growing-degree hardness theorem.

## 5. Distortion Is Unavoidable For This Entire Lift Class

The simple positive lift is not uniquely at fault. Let r be the coefficient-
centered real residue of -M*bar(M), and S=||r||^2. For EVERY real totally
positive lift rho=r mod q, centering minimizes each coefficient magnitude,
so ||rho||^2>=S. Also trace(C_rho^2)/d=||rho||^2. Consequently

```
lambda_max(C_rho)^2 >= S,
condition_number(diag(I,C_rho))^2 >= S.
```

The identity block matters: this is not cured by uniformly rescaling the norm.
It is a worst-case metric distortion bound, NOT a bound on every vector or on
the success of every weighted-short algorithm. Different coordinate maps and
algorithms giving stronger output guarantees remain outside the statement.

For the high-CRT IID source, M=(a,b) with independent uniform a,b in E; its
real norm a*b is exactly a mixture of a uniform real residue with weight
alpha=1-1/|E| and a point mass at zero with weight 1/|E|. Uniform centered
real residues have h=d/2 independent integer coordinates: one with weight one
and h-1 with weight two; the middle coefficient is zero. Put

```
mu2=(q^2-1)/12, mu4=(q^2-1)*(3q^2-7)/240,
mu=E_uniform(S)=(d-1)*mu2,
v=Var_uniform(S)=(2d-3)*(mu4-mu2^2).
```

The native moments are alpha*mu and alpha*(v+mu^2), not the naive uniform
moments. Chebyshev and the exact mixture imply

```
Pr_native[S>=mu/2] >= alpha*max(0,1-4v/mu^2).
```

Thus with probability 1-O(1/d)-1/|E|, EVERY positive congruence lift in these
graph coordinates has metric condition number at least
sqrt((d-1)*(q^2-1)/24). At d64 the conservative bound exceeds 0.89.
Complete finite-source moments are independently checked alongside counts.
The d2 distribution is deliberately excluded. These facts strengthen the
metric-transfer proof obligation, not a universal quantum impossibility claim.

## 6. Norm-One Units Do Not Improve Fixed-Norm Generators Here

For the ACTUALLY CONSTRUCTED order, C_rho>=I. If u=(g,f) has nrd(u)=1,
taking the normalized trace gives ||g||^2+f^T C_rho f=1. Integrality then
forces exactly one block to be a signed monomial and the other zero. The
f-only branch has reduced norm rho, so is possible only when rho=1.

Hence norm-one units are exactly the 2d signed R monomials if rho!=1,
and those plus their j multiples (4d total) if rho=1. Their actions preserve
original physical length. Outside the rho=1 branch they preserve the same
R-projective direction as well. Two generators of the same principal left
ideal with the SAME reduced norm differ by such a norm-one unit: write
alpha_2=u*alpha_1 using equality of the ideals and use multiplicativity.
Thus searching these units cannot shorten a fixed-reduced-norm generator.

This is not a classification of units with other reduced norms, maximal
overorders with fractional coordinates, every positive lift, or quaternion
algorithms that find non-generating short elements. Those routes remain open.
Bounded d2 controls enumerate the actual norm-one units and fixed-norm orbits;
the enumeration is exponential calibration, not a purported fast search.

## 7. Literature and Remaining Obligations

[EPRINT-2025-287](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/287) gives a rank-two module-LIP
reduction to a quaternion principal-ideal variant, nonuniform in general and
uniform for Hawk. That is not a native random graph-kernel SVP reduction or an
efficient quaternion generator algorithm. Current primary abstract was checked;
the earlier full [2024/1147 PDF](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1147.pdf) was read,
not the merged 2025 full proof. Preserve that version distinction.

2026-10-30 update: the full merged 2025-02-19 paper has now been read and
cached. [QUATERNION_NORM_SLICE_AND_LOCAL_FLAGS.md](QUATERNION_NORM_SLICE_AND_LOCAL_FLAGS.md)
records its exact norm-constrained RIGHT-ideal input and uniform/nonuniform
reduction scopes, superseding the abstract-only evidence status above.
It does not turn this native random graph kernel into a Hawk instance.
The [separate HSVP audit](QUATERNION_HSVP_PREPRINT_AUDIT.md) retains both
metric and actual membership checks for later short-vector proposals.

The earlier full-paper audit of
[EPRINT-2025-1095](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1095) notes that quaternion
generator discovery remains unresolved and that exhaustive ideal/four-square
enumeration does not supply an efficient algorithm. The PDF endpoint currently
returns 403 on a refresh. This is not a cryptographic hardness theorem.

Highest-value next work:

1. Study the definite LEFT ideal as an actual short-element problem; prove its
   source distribution, order presentation cost and metric distortion. Do not
   assume principality or a known reduced-norm promise where none is supplied.
2. A different positive lift ALONE cannot evade the bound above. Seek a new
   coordinate construction, or a short-element guarantee strong enough to
   overcome that distortion on the actual source. Prove rather than assume
   the source and geometric transfer of either alternative.
3. Any proposed quantum generator must specify a physical input, precision,
   gate/query complexity, success probability and final original-metric output.
4. Try to kill the output with native lattice reduction and ordinary short
   element baselines. Successful bounded algebra identities are not advantage.
5. For a new useful relation, charge its existing kernel-ideal completion,
   projective direction, index, Gram height and reciprocal-energy obligations.

## 8. Verification and Handoff

Module/tests: `theorems/native_rlwe_quaternion_kernel.py` and
`tests/test_native_rlwe_quaternion_kernel.py`. Report:
`research/reductions/native_rlwe_quaternion_kernel.json`. Independent BigInt
checker: `research/certificates/native_rlwe_quaternion_kernel_crosscheck.js`.
Finite identities and two implementations are NOT independent theorem review.

Gemini owns production CLI/registry/full-suite integration. The research
contract is unaccepted; keep negative conclusions scoped to their hypothesis
class, keep positive encoding separate from generator success, and do not
promote source-gate or small-control evidence to a speedup claim.

derivations.heading: Polynomial Decoder Certificate And The OPI Equivalence
derivations.text:
The next hard check replaces an assumed exponential ML table by a specified
polynomial classical decoder at the theorem level. This is an analytic
certificate, NOT execution of a quantum state or a new implementation of GS.
[Chatterjee--Harsha--Kumar, Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.05176v2)
supplies deterministic list decoding in poly(L,log p) at integer agreement
t>sqrt(L*(r-1)). It avoids a hidden randomized-factorization assumption for
coherent decoding over large prime fields. The local application still needs
independent review and a full quantum precision/resource contract.

### A Decoder With No Hidden List-Selection Advice

List every degree<r polynomial agreeing with the received word at least t
times. Choose greatest agreement, canonical ties, and label0 if the list is
empty. Do not ask for the true message or original target to select a list item.

For p3mod4 the actual product chirp readout is memoryless q-ary symmetric:
q0>1/2 and each particular wrong symbol has q1<1/(2*(p-1)). For ANY transmitted
codeword, bound its probability of fewer than t correct positions by

```text
E_true <= 2^(-L) * sum_(j=0)^(t-1) binom(L,j).
```

Any other degree<r polynomial agrees with the true one on at most r-1
positions. To obtain t agreements it needs u=t-r+1 accidental matches.
Independence and a union bound over position subsets and ALL other words give

```text
E_wrong <= (p^r-1)*binom(L,u) / [2*(p-1)]^u,
epsilon <= min(1,E_true+E_wrong).
```

No words are enumerated by this calculation. If the true word reaches t and
no other word does, selection is uniquely correct. The bound holds for every
basis label, and the earlier full-channel identity consequently gives
uniform-target mean paid ORIGINAL validity >=max(0,1-2*epsilon). It is not a
worst-target guarantee. For any fixed rate R<1/4 choose sqrt(R)<t/L<1/2;
then t/L>2R, so the true-word tail is exp(-Omega(L)) and the competitor bound
is exp(-Omega(L log p)) as L grows with L<p. This is an algorithmic reduction
using known decoding results, not evidence for classical hardness or novelty.

The v5 artifact evaluates exact rational bounds, rounded OUTWARD to96 dyadic
bits. Rounding a very small positive bound upward is deliberate, never0.
At p=2^61-1:

| L | r | t | Decoder-error upper bound (approximate display) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 64 | 200 | 2.67e-7 |
| 1024 | 128 | 400 | 8.36e-13 |

These are symbolic guarantees under the ideal specified instrument, not runs
at those quantum register counts. A uniform full-flagged implementation trace
error delta must be subtracted from the mean validity bound. For p3mod4 a
public nonsquare can be -1, not an assumed free nonresidue search; local C
can be built using reversible squaring, canonical modular square roots and
a conditional Hadamard on the root sign. Source/QFT phases, approximate
uniform field states, reversible decoder workspace cleanup and total error
still require an explicit costed implementation. Tests/report gates keep
those obligations OPEN. No central proof or candidate is promoted.

### This Is An Existing OPI Route In Different Coordinates

Before treating that mechanism as new, apply standard GRS duality. For ANY
distinct support S, construct the same target lift B but without dividing b by
kappa. Then all solutions z to sum a^k*z_a=b_k are EXACTLY

```text
z_a=(B(a)+P(a))/A'(a),    deg(P)<K=L-r.
```

The inclusion follows from quadrature on degree<=L-2 polynomials; equality
follows since the nullspace and the polynomial space both have dimension K.
The native square problem is therefore OPI with public shift -B(a),
orientation equal to the quadratic character of A'(a), and degree bound K.
Square-root each accepted native z_a to recover x_a in the ORIGINAL field.
Conversely, interpolating A'(a)*x_a^2-B(a) gives such a degree<K polynomial
for every native solution. This is a bijection on square-coordinate solutions,
not necessarily on their multiple choices of square-root signs.

Thus r/L<1/4 is a HIGH-RATE K/L>3/4 explicit-character OPI problem, not an
independent new quantum primitive. The [soft-decoder framework](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.12553v2)
already supplies the relevant inhomogeneous reduction paradigm. Its stated
full-support convention is not a reason to overlook GRS-dual weights on a
punctured input. A new name does not remove the repo's classical OPI attacks.

The new wrapper calls the EXISTING norm solver, without editing or replacing
it, on one fixed p=2^61-1, S=(1,...,127), r31 input. The equivalent OPI has
K96,56 square orientations and71 nonsquare orientations. Public seed6611 and
cap128 produce a perfect OPI witness in16 charged base-field factorizations,
then127 native square roots satisfy ALL31 original moment equations. All127
coordinates happen to be nonzero; the control did not request a strict-mode
population guarantee. Every rejected norm target and the winning polynomial
are saved. This refutes the finite control as advantage evidence, NOT every
target, every sparse input or the old folded extension-norm problem.

### A Correct Average-Case Transfer, With An Important Limit

There is a further exact distinction from the old fixed-input norm analysis.
Let b be uniform in F_p^r and let M be an INDEPENDENT uniform polynomial of
degree<K. The high-r-coefficient triangular construction of B_b and the low-K
coefficient space are complementary. Therefore

```text
(b,M) -> B_b+M -> its L evaluations -> negative OPI shifts
```

is a linear bijection onto F_p^L: the induced shifts really ARE IID uniform.
Adding M preserves the native syndrome, since it is in the kernel. Running
OPI on shifts -(B_b+M) and recovering x from (B_b+M+P)/A' never rerolls the
original b. Consequently the existing norm attack's one-trial IID population
lower bound transfers to UNIFORM native targets plus independent kernel masks,
when its explicit degree and field hypotheses hold. For the above support,
D72 and K96 meet those hypotheses; the exact lower bound I_p(72)/p^72 is
saved. The seeded fixed-input witness did NOT execute that population process.

For a FIXED b, random M reaches only p^K shifts, not p^L; it is not IID.
Also E_b[q(b)]>=1/poly does NOT prove high-probability success on most b,
nor justify replacing E_b[(1-q(b))^T] by (1-E_b q(b))^T. This removes a claim
of negligible classical population success but does not fully match the
quantum mean bound. The distribution of q(b), rather than more finite seeds,
is the next meaningful probability question. All source/IID/amplification
gates remain explicit and independent review is pending.

FOLLOW-UP: [native-variable masking](MOMENT_TARGET_MASKING.md) now BYPASSES
that probability gap for certified splits, rather than claiming the old
unmasked q(b) is well behaved. It reserves ORIGINAL coordinates, uses their
exact MDS/Gauss near-uniform moment law, then applies a kernel mask and the
existing norm solver to the residual target. At the same p61,L127,r31,
reserving32 coordinates yields a local fixed-b floor>=0.0208117541, with two

central negative.

budget was not justified. DCP still lacks a new constructive receiver; generic

quadratic-source erasure problem without making native search classically easy?

coordinate, retains the original square constraints, and uses outer coding.
The direct full-field Reed--Solomon realization fails the search-advantage
test: a deterministic classical construction below solves EVERY target in
the entire proposed useful rate range, and beyond. Retain the local primitive
and counteralgorithm; do not build a large quantum compiler for this family.

withdraws its state-preparation theorem because its per-register step has
exponentially small joint success. That is motivation to examine a new route,


### A Decoder With No Hidden List-Selection Advice

List every degree<r polynomial agreeing with the received word at least t
times. Choose greatest agreement, canonical ties, and label0 if the list is
empty. Do not ask for the true message or original target to select a list item.

For p3mod4 the actual product chirp readout is memoryless q-ary symmetric:
q0>1/2 and each particular wrong symbol has q1<1/(2*(p-1)). For ANY transmitted
codeword, bound its probability of fewer than t correct positions by

```text
E_true <= 2^(-L) * sum_(j=0)^(t-1) binom(L,j).
```

Any other degree<r polynomial agrees with the true one on at most r-1
positions. To obtain t agreements it needs u=t-r+1 accidental matches.
Independence and a union bound over position subsets and ALL other words give

```text
E_wrong <= (p^r-1)*binom(L,u) / [2*(p-1)]^u,
epsilon <= min(1,E_true+E_wrong).
```

No words are enumerated by this calculation. If the true word reaches t and
no other word does, selection is uniquely correct. The bound holds for every
basis label, and the earlier full-channel identity consequently gives
uniform-target mean paid ORIGINAL validity >=max(0,1-2*epsilon). It is not a
worst-target guarantee. For any fixed rate R<1/4 choose sqrt(R)<t/L<1/2;

is exp(-Omega(L log p)) as L grows with L<p. This is an algorithmic reduction
